description: Trigger a restart of this solet with the new manifest active. Called by lifecycle_management_service::apply_manifest AFTER the new manifest has been validated and written to disk; the bound self-deployment plugin executes the actual restart. Cloud profile binds this to aws_self_deployment_plugin, which runs the 12-step blue-green ECS swap with the new manifest in place (same image, new env) and returns RestartStatus.QUEUED with the finisher action id so the operator can poll cutover via cloud_self_deployment_service::deploy_status. macOS profile binds this to macos_self_deployment_plugin, which runs the router-mediated blue/green swap — spawning the next color via python -m ananta.cli, polling the router until green registers, swapping atomically via the router, and quiescing blue for the drain window. The verb is sync — backgrounding is the caller's concern via scheduling_service::execute_in_seconds. The verb does NOT re-validate the manifest — apply_manifest's pre-flight is authoritative — and the on-disk manifest is the source of truth for the new boot. The expected_etag parameter is a CAS lock: implementations re-read the manifest's stored ETag at dispatch time and refuse the restart when it differs, guarding against a second apply_manifest racing the first between manifest-write and restart-dispatch.
embedding_description: Restart this solet to pick up the manifest apply_manifest just wrote to disk. Cloud sibling runs blue-green ECS swap; macOS sibling runs router-mediated blue/green swap. Generic surface — platform asks 'restart', the bound plugin decides 'how'. expected_etag CAS-locks against the on-disk manifest. Returns RestartResult: status, restart_action_id, reason, expected_etag, dry_run.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: RestartResult frozen dataclass with attributes: status (RestartStatus value — 'queued' for async cutover, 'completed' for synchronous restart, 'failed' when the restart could not be scheduled), restart_action_id (non-empty when status='queued'; cloud sibling returns a pollable identifier consumable by cloud_self_deployment_service::deploy_status; macOS sibling returns an audit-only synthetic token because the action that is restarting is the very one being killed and no platform action-queue row backs it), message (human-readable status detail), reason (echoes the operator-supplied reason for audit), expected_etag (echoes the CAS-lock etag the caller asserted), dry_run (echoes the dry_run flag).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: When status='queued', surface restart_action_id so the operator can poll deployment-specific status verbs (cloud_self_deployment_service::deploy_status for cloud). When status='completed', confirm the new manifest is active. When status='failed', surface the error message and recommend re-running apply_manifest after the underlying issue is resolved. When dry_run=True, the response describes the planned restart without having executed it.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Restart the live solet with a manifest that was just written to disk by apply_manifest.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: self_deployment_service_unavailable: no plugin is bound to self_deployment_service (apply_manifest's pre-flight should have caught this). manifest_not_on_disk: the caller did not write the manifest before invoking — apply_manifest contract violation. precondition_failed: the on-disk manifest's stored ETag has shifted since the caller observed expected_etag — a concurrent apply_manifest raced this one between write and restart-dispatch. restart_failed: the bound implementation could not schedule the restart (cloud: blue-green pre-flight failed; macOS: watchdog could not fork).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: self_deployment_service_unavailable: fix service_bindings.json then call apply_manifest again. manifest_not_on_disk: do not call restart_with_manifest directly; route through apply_manifest. precondition_failed: re-read the current manifest via apply_manifest(dry_run=True) to fetch the fresh current_etag, then re-submit apply_manifest with that as expected_etag. restart_failed: surface the underlying message — cloud-side issues are typically AWS-state mismatches resolvable by re-running deploy_self with the same image_tag (idempotent); macOS-side issues are typically subprocess.Popen failures resolvable by checking launch.py's interpreter path.
